title: Set greeting expressions
pattern: fixed phrases (learn each as a whole)
meaning_en: Greetings are fixed expressions; the polite form adds ございます or ます endings.
explanation: Japanese greetings are fixed phrases: learn each one as a whole rather than word by word. They also change with the time of day and with how polite you need to be.
Many casual greetings have a polite form made by adding ございます: おはよう (casual) becomes おはようございます (polite), and ありがとう becomes ありがとうございます.
The は in こんにちは and こんばんは is pronounced "wa". It is a spelling convention left over from the past.
structure_notes: Casual: おはよう, ありがとう. Polite: おはようございます, ありがとうございます.
common_mistakes: Saying おはよう to a stranger or a boss (use おはようございます).
Reading こんにちは as "konnichiha": it is "konnichiwa".
